messages.text: My nerdoctaxe 3.1 just stopped hashing.  Fans still power on but screen is dead and no hashing.

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

Fans spinning but a dead screen can be anything from the display ribbon to the board, so let's narrow it fast.

First check: can you still reach the miner's web interface?

1. Open your router's client list (or an app like Fing) and look for the NerdOctaxe / "nerdqaxe" / "bitaxe" entry.
2. If you find it, type that IP into a browser.

Tell me which happens:
- the web UI loads (and what hashrate and ASIC temp it shows), or
- the device does not appear on the network at all.

That one answer tells me whether the board is alive with just a dead display, or the board itself has dropped out.

Thanks, that narrows it: fans turn but the board is not booting (no screen, no network). On these boards that points at the power supply first, since the fans run off the raw input and will spin even when the board is not getting clean enough power to come up.

Next check: do you have a second power supply you can try, matching the rating printed on your current brick (same voltage, same or higher amps)?

1. Unplug the unit.
2. Swap in the other brick, straight into the wall, no power strip or extension.
3. Plug it back in and watch for 60 seconds.

Tell me what the label on your current brick says (volts and amps) and what the unit does with the second one: screen still dead, or does it come up?
screen still dead, mean well RSP-1500 power supply 12.3 v
Let me confirm the correct input voltage for the NerdOctaxe 3.1 before I say anything about that supply.
Searched the web · NerdOctaxe 3.1 input voltage DC specification

Checked the board specs: the NerdOctaxe family is a 
12 V board with a four-phase TPS546 regulator stack
, so your 12.3 V rail is in range. Nothing fried from voltage there. 12.3 V is a touch high for comfort (12.0 V is the sweet spot) but it is not what is keeping it dark.

Important: swapping the barrel lead from one output of the same RSP-1500 is not a second power supply. The rail has to be proven good independently.

So, next check, pick whichever is easier:

1. Is another miner running right now off that same RSP-1500? If yes, the rail is proven and we can rule it out.
2. Or plug the NerdOctaxe into the stock 12 V brick it shipped with (or any good 12 V supply rated 15 A or more), straight to the wall.

While you do that, tell me one more thing: with power applied, is there ANY sign of life on the board besides the fans? A small LED lit on the controller board, the screen backlight faintly glowing, anything.
When i pull the screen off and plug it into a usb from computer it powers on

That is a useful result. It means the display module (the T-Display-S3 controller) is fine, it boots happily on USB 5 V. So this is not a dead screen. What is dead is the 5 V the main board is supposed to send up to that module when it runs on 12 V.

Two things can cause that: the 12 V rail is not actually arriving at the board under load, or the board's own step-down has failed.

So the one test left to separate them:

1. Put the display module back on the board.
2. Power the board from a known-good 12 V supply (the stock brick, or another 12 V 15 A+ supply), not the RSP-1500 output you have been using, straight to the wall.
3. Watch 60 seconds.

If you have a multimeter, even better: with the RSP-1500 connected and the fans spinning, measure DC volts right at the board's power input pads or barrel. Tell me the reading.

While that runs, please send me two things so I do not have to ask twice:
- a short video of the unit from plug-in through the first 30 seconds
- a clear photo of the serial number sticker
yes i have 3 Nexus S1.2 and 3 NerdQaxe++4.8 and a BS-2 being powered by power supply

Good, that tells me a lot. Those seven units are the load test: if the Nexus S1s, the NerdQaxe++s and the BS-2 are all running normally right now off that same RSP-1500, the rail is proven good and we can strike the power supply off the list.

Confirm that for me: are all seven up and hashing at this moment?

If they are, here is where that leaves your NerdOctaxe. The fans spin, which proves 12 V is reaching the board through its lead. The display module boots on USB, which proves the module is good. So 12 V goes in, and the board is not producing the 5 V that feeds the controller. That is on the board itself, not the supply, not the screen, not the firmware.

One thing to be careful of in the meantime: at 12.3 V you are at the top of the window. Trimming the RSP-1500 down to a flat 12.0 V is kinder to the other seven boards. Do that from the external adjustment, never with the case open.

Still need from you, and then I can put this in front of our hardware lead with everything he needs:
- a short video from plug-in through the first 30 seconds
- a clear photo of the serial number sticker
yes all the other ones are still powered on and hashing

That settles it. The rail is proven good under seven other miners, so the supply is cleared.

Summary of where we are: 12 V reaches your NerdOctaxe (fans spin), the display module is good (boots on USB), but the board produces no 5 V for the controller, so nothing boots, no screen, no network, no hashing. That is a board-level failure, not a setting, not firmware, not the screen, not the PSU.

Two last things so I can hand this over complete:

1. A clear photo of the serial number sticker on the unit (a short clip of the plug-in is a bonus, not required at this point).
2. Which of your orders this NerdOctaxe came on. You have several with us and I do not want to attach the wrong one.

Send those and I will put the full findings in front of JD, our hardware lead, straight away.
Verdict recorded and the chat is back with Sarah.
